---
title: "Spatial analysis of a field trial"
author: "Dongwen Luo"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 3.5)
```

```{r setup}
library(predictmeans)
library(nlme)
library(ggplot2)
```

Plots next to each other in a field are often more alike than plots far apart. A model that ignores this
gives standard errors that are wrong. This article checks a trial for it with `residvariogram()`, then fits
the two usual spatial models: a separable AR1 x AR1 correlation (`corAR1xAR1()`) and a smooth trend over the
field (`t2(row, col)` in `semireg()`).

The Slate Hall Farm trial (Genstat's REML Guide, chapter 3): 25 wheat varieties in 6 replicates, 150 plots
on a grid of 10 field rows by 15 field columns.

```{r}
d <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "slatehall.csv", package = "predictmeans"))
d$variety <- factor(d$variety)
d$rep <- factor(d$replicates)
d$rowf <- factor(d$fieldrow)
d$colf <- factor(d$fieldcolumn)
```

## 1. The randomized complete block analysis and its variogram

```{r}
m0 <- lm(yield ~ rep + variety, data = d)
v0 <- residvariogram(m0, row = "fieldrow", col = "fieldcolumn", data = d)
advice(v0)$text
```

```{r, fig.height = 4}
autoplot(v0)
```

The variogram is below its envelope at the shortest lags: neighbouring plots are more alike than the block
model allows, and the advice says what to fit.

## 2. AR1 x AR1 over the field

```{r}
fA <- gls(yield ~ variety, data = d, correlation = corAR1xAR1(form = ~ fieldrow + fieldcolumn))
coef(fA$modelStruct$corStruct, unconstrained = FALSE)
fB <- gls(yield ~ variety, data = d,
          correlation = corAR1xAR1(form = ~ fieldrow + fieldcolumn, nugget = TRUE))
coef(fB$modelStruct$corStruct, unconstrained = FALSE)
anova(fA, fB)
```

The nugget (an independent plot error besides the AR1 x AR1 part) improves the fit (REML deviance 7.0
lower). Its variogram stays inside the envelope:

```{r, fig.height = 4}
vB <- residvariogram(fB, row = "fieldrow", col = "fieldcolumn", data = d, nsim = 39)
advice(vB)$text
autoplot(vB)
```

The variety means and their comparisons, with Kenward-Roger df:

```{r}
pB <- predictmeans(fB, "variety")
head(pB$means[, c("variety", "estimate", "std.error", "df")])
summary(pB$pairs$std.error)
```

A single mean has a large SE with few df (about 1.0 on 4.6 df here): with strong correlation along the
field (phi 0.84 between columns) the field's overall level is poorly known. Comparisons do not depend on it,
and their SEDs (mean 0.62) are much smaller than those of the block analysis (1.07, below).

Replicates can be added as random effects. In `lme()` a correlation acts only within the groups of the
innermost random effect, so for an AR1 x AR1 over the whole field the replicate effects go in one group:

```{r}
d$all <- factor(1)
fD <- lme(yield ~ variety, random = list(all = pdIdent(~ rep - 1)), data = d,
          correlation = corAR1xAR1(form = ~ fieldrow + fieldcolumn | all, nugget = TRUE))
VarCorr(fD)[1:2, ]
```

Here the replicate variance is estimated as 0 (Genstat, which allows negative components, gives -0.078), so
the model is the same as `fB`.

Several trials are analysed together with `form = ~ row + col | trial` (the same phi in every trial), or
with `by_group = TRUE` a phi pair for each trial and, through `varIdent()`, a residual variance for each:

```r
gls(yield ~ trial / variety, data = trials, weights = varIdent(form = ~ 1 | trial),
    correlation = corAR1xAR1(form = ~ row + col | trial, by_group = TRUE))
```

This gives each trial the estimates and SEDs of its own fit (checked in the tests), with the means of all
trials in one table.

## 3. A smooth trend over the field

```{r}
fT <- semireg(yield ~ variety + t2(fieldrow, fieldcolumn) + (1 | rowf) + (1 | colf), data = d)
pT <- predictmeans(fT, "variety")
```

A smooth surface over the field, as SpATS fits, with random row and column effects: often as good as AR1 x
AR1 in practice. On this trial the AR1 x AR1 fit gives the more precise means:

```{r}
sed <- function(p) mean(p$pairs$std.error)
data.frame(model = c("blocks (lm)", "AR1 x AR1 + nugget", "t2 trend"),
           mean_SED = c(sed(predictmeans(m0, "variety")), sed(pB), sed(pT)))
```

## Checks

`corAR1xAR1()` was checked against a Genstat run of these models (`dev/genstat/ar1ar1-slatehall.gen`):

| | predictmeans / nlme | Genstat |
|---|---|---|
| AR1 x AR1: phi row, column | 0.4586, 0.6838 | 0.4586, 0.6838 |
| with nugget: phi; units variance | 0.6827, 0.8438; 0.486 | 0.6827, 0.8438; 0.486 |
| REML deviance difference | 7.00 | 7.00 |
| 25 means and 300 SEDs of each model | within 1e-6 | |
| variety F test d.d.f. (`df_method = "KR-average"`) | 79.99, 75.67 | 80.0, 75.7 |

The SEDs agree with `vcov_adjust = FALSE` (Genstat's are not adjusted); the default Kenward-Roger
adjusted SEs are slightly larger. The tests are in `tests/testthat/test-cor-ar1xar1.R`.

## References

- Gilmour, A. R., Cullis, B. R. and Verbyla, A. P. (1997). Accounting for natural and extraneous variation in
  the analysis of field experiments. *Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics*, 2,
  269-293.
- Rodríguez-Álvarez, M. X., Boer, M. P., van Eeuwijk, F. A. and Eilers, P. H. C. (2018). Correcting for
  spatial heterogeneity in plant breeding experiments with P-splines. *Spatial Statistics*, 23, 52-71.
